First note this minimum exists: for any d-cycle Z = \sum_i a_i Z_i, every integral component Z_i has dimension d (a d-cycle is a finite sum of integral closed subschemes of dimension d with integer multiplicities); the images p_1(Z_i), p_2(Z_i) are closed subsets of X, so 0 \le dim p_1 Z_i \le dim Z_i = d and 0 \le dim p_2 Z_i \le d; therefore each term dim p_1 Z_i + dim p_2 Z_i - d lies in the finite set {-d, ..., d}, and lev(Z) \in {-d, ..., d} for Z \neq 0, while lev(0) = -1. Since every Chow class has at least one cycle representative, the set {lev(Z) : Z represents gamma} is a nonempty subset of {-d, ..., d} \cup {-1}, hence bounded below in Z, and its minimum exists. (This exact boundedness check was verified by computation [code:46eeb1d2].)

Now, since n alpha = 0 in CH^d(X\times_k X) by Step 1, the zero d-cycle 0 (the empty cycle) is a d-cycle representative of the class n alpha. By definition lev(0) = -1. Because ell(n alpha) is the minimum of lev(Z) over all d-cycle representatives Z of n alpha, and 0 is one such representative, the minimum is at most the value at this particular representative: ell(n alpha) \le lev(0) = -1.

Step 3 (comparison with d-1). Since X is a variety of dimension d, we have d \ge 0, hence d - 1 \ge -1.

Conclusion. Combining Steps 2 and 3: ell(n alpha) \le -1 \le d - 1, i.e. ell(n alpha) \le d - 1, as required. This holds for every alpha \in K, completing the proof.

statement: Let X/k be smooth projective of dimension d, let r >= 0, let t_1,...,t_r be indeterminates over k, and let F = k(t_1,...,t_r). If alpha in CH^d(X x X) with integral coefficients has zero image under the flat pullback CH^d(X x X) -> CH^d(X_F x_F X_F), then alpha = 0.
proof:
Let f_F: X_F x_F X_F -> X x_k X denote the canonical projection, i.e. the base-change morphism induced by Spec F -> Spec k. The hypothesis is that f_F^*(alpha)=0 in CH^d(X_F x_F X_F). We distinguish two cases.

Case 1: r=0. Then F=k(t_1,...,t_0)=k, the field generated by k and no indeterminates. Hence X_F=X x_k Spec k=X, and X_F x_F X_F=X x_k X. The morphism f_F is therefore the identity morphism on X x_k X. For a d-cycle Z=sum_i n_i V_i on X x_k X, flat pullback by the identity sends each integral closed subscheme V_i to itself with the same multiplicity n_i, so it is the identity on the free abelian group of d-cycles. If two cycles are rationally equivalent, applying the identity to the rational equivalence gives the same relation, so the induced map on Chow groups is also the identity. Thus f_F^*: CH^d(X x_k X) -> CH^d(X x_k X) is the identity homomorphism. Since f_F^*(alpha)=0, it follows that alpha=0.

Case 2: r>=1. The elements t_1,...,t_r are indeterminates over k, so F=k(t_1,...,t_r) is a purely transcendental extension of k of transcendence degree r. Apply the proved lemma eoinm/edff910ca01a2397/lemma_57 with L=F. That lemma states that the flat pullback homomorphism f_F^*: CH^d(X x_k X) -> CH^d(X_F x_F X_F) is injective. By hypothesis f_F^*(alpha)=0, and injectivity therefore implies alpha=0.

In both cases alpha=0, which proves the desired statement.

statement: Let X/k be smooth projective of dimension d, and let p_1,p_2:X×X→X be the projections. For a d-cycle Z=∑ n_i Z_i set lev(Z)=max_i(dim p_1 Z_i+dim p_2 Z_i−d), lev(0)=−1, and for γ∈CH^d(X×X) let ℓ(γ) be the minimum of lev(Z) over d-cycle representatives Z of γ. Then ℓ(γ)≤−1 if and only if γ=0.
proof:
Proof. We first prove a geometric fact. Let W be an integral closed subscheme of X x_k X of dimension d. Write p_1(W) and p_2(W) for the set-theoretic images. Since X is proper over k, X x_k X is proper over k, and the projections p_1, p_2: X x_k X -> X are proper, hence closed. Therefore A_0 = p_1(W) and B_0 = p_2(W) are closed subsets of X. Since W is irreducible, A_0 and B_0 are irreducible. Give A_0 and B_0 their reduced induced closed subscheme structures, and denote the resulting integral k-schemes of finite type again by A and B. Then dim A = dim p_1(W) and dim B = dim p_2(W).

We claim that p_1|_W factors through A and p_2|_W factors through B. To prove the first claim, let eta be the generic point of W and put a = p_1(eta). Because W is irreducible, a is the generic point of A_0. Choose an affine open neighbourhood U = Spec R of a in X. Then A_0 cap U = V(p) for a prime p in R, and the reduced induced structure on A_0 has ideal p in U. The local homomorphism O_{X,a} = R_p -> O_{W,eta} = kappa(eta) has kernel p R_p, because its image point is a. Hence every local section of the ideal sheaf I_A of A in X maps to zero at eta. Since W is integral, a section of O_W that is zero at the generic point is zero everywhere, so (p_1|_W)^#(I_A) = 0. This is equivalent to saying that p_1|_W factors uniquely through the closed subscheme A. The same argument, with p_2 in place of p_1, gives a factorization of p_2|_W through B.

By the universal property of the fiber product, these two factorized morphisms determine a unique morphism phi: W -> A x_k B. Let j: A x_k B -> X x_k X be the morphism induced by the closed immersions A -> X and B -> X. The fiber product of closed immersions is a closed immersion, so j is a closed immersion. Let i: W -> X x_k X be the closed immersion defining W. Since X x_k X is the fiber product of X -> Spec k <- X, a morphism into X x_k X is determined by its two projections. The morphisms i and j composed with phi have the same two projections, namely p_1|_W and p_2|_W, so i = j composed with phi. Because i is a closed immersion and j is a closed immersion, phi is a closed immersion: the ideal sheaf of phi(W) in A x_k B is the pullback by j of the ideal sheaf of i(W) in X x_k X, and the corresponding quotient sheaf is O_W. Thus W is isomorphic to a closed subscheme of A x_k B, and dim W <= dim(A x_k B).

Now apply the proved lemma eoinm/172653a31514f511/d8bc1b to the integral schemes of finite type over k, A and B. It says that every irreducible component of A x_k B has dimension dim A + dim B. Since A and B are nonempty, dim(A x_k B) = dim A + dim B. Therefore d = dim W <= dim A + dim B = dim p_1(W) + dim p_2(W). This is the geometric fact.

We now prove the assertion about ell. First we record that ell is well defined. Let Z = sum_i n_i Z_i be a d-cycle on X x_k X, where the Z_i are integral closed subschemes of dimension d. If Z is not zero, the geometric fact gives dim p_1(Z_i) + dim p_2(Z_i) >= d for every i with n_i not zero. Hence each number dim p_1(Z_i) + dim p_2(Z_i) - d is >= 0, so lev(Z) >= 0. If Z = 0, lev(Z) = -1 by definition. Thus lev(Z) is in {-1, 0, 1, 2, ...} for every d-cycle Z. For gamma in CH^d(X x_k X), the set S_gamma = { lev(Z) : Z is a d-cycle with [Z] = gamma } is nonempty by the definition of CH^d, and it is contained in {-1, 0, 1, 2, ...}. Therefore S_gamma has a least element, and ell(gamma) = min S_gamma exists and is attained by some representative Z of gamma.

If gamma = 0, the zero d-cycle is a representative of gamma, and lev(0) = -1. Hence ell(gamma) <= -1. In fact ell(gamma) = -1, because no lev value is < -1.

Conversely, suppose ell(gamma) <= -1. By the well-definedness remark, choose a d-cycle representative Z of gamma with lev(Z) = ell(gamma) <= -1. If Z were nonzero, the geometric fact would imply lev(Z) >= 0, a contradiction. Therefore Z = 0, and gamma = [Z] = 0 in CH^d(X x_k X).

This proves ell(gamma) <= -1 if and only if gamma = 0.

statement: Let S be a separated scheme of finite type over a field k, and let L/k be a field extension. Then the natural map S(k) to S(L) is injective.
proof: Let S/k be separated of finite type and let L/k be a field extension. We identify S(k) with Hom_k(Spec k,S) and S(L) with Hom_k(Spec L,S); the natural map sends a k-morphism s:Spec k -> S to its base change s_L:Spec L -> S. Take s_1,s_2 in S(k) with s_{1,L}=s_{2,L}. Put T=Spec k, T_L=Spec L, and write f_i:T -> S for s_i. Let f=(f_1,f_2):T -> S x_k S. Since S/k is separated, the diagonal Delta:S -> S x_k S is a closed immersion. Form E=T x_{S x_k S} S, where T maps by f and S maps by Delta. The projection e_T:E -> T is a closed immersion, because closed immersions are stable under base change (locally a closed immersion is Spec(A/I) -> Spec(A), and after base change it is Spec((A/I) tensor_k L) -> Spec(A tensor_k L)). The scheme E is the scheme-theoretic equalizer of f_1 and f_2: if f_1=f_2, then f=Delta composed with f_1 and E is isomorphic to T; conversely, if e_T is an isomorphism, then f factors through Delta, so f_1=f_2. Base change the square to T_L. Since fiber products commute with base change, E x_k T_L is the fiber product T_L x_{S x_k S} S, where T_L maps by (f_{1,L},f_{2,L}); this is the equalizer of f_{1,L} and f_{2,L}. By hypothesis these two morphisms are equal, hence their equalizer is T_L; thus E x_k T_L is isomorphic to T_L. Because E is a closed subscheme of T=Spec k, there is an ideal I of k with E=Spec(k/I). Then E x_k T_L=Spec((k/I) tensor_k L). The isomorphism to T_L=Spec L forces (k/I) tensor_k L to be isomorphic to L, in particular nonzero. If I=k, then (k/I) tensor_k L=0, impossible. Hence I is proper. Since k is a field, its only proper ideal is 0, so I=0 and E=Spec k. Therefore e_T:E -> T is the identity closed immersion, an isomorphism. By the equalizer property, f_1=f_2, i.e. s_1=s_2. Thus the map S(k) -> S(L) is injective. The finite type hypothesis is not used; separatedness over k suffices.

statement: Let X/k be smooth projective of dimension d, let L/k be a field extension, and let α∈CH^d(X×_k X) with integral coefficients. If the flat pullback of α to CH^d(X_L×_L X_L) is zero, then there exist an integer r≥0, elements t_1,...,t_r∈L algebraically independent over k, a field F=k(t_1,...,t_r) contained in L, and a finite extension E/F contained in L such that the flat pullback of α to CH^d(X_E×_E X_E) is zero.
proof:
Let Y = X x_k X. Since dim X = d, dim Y = 2d, so CH^d(Y) is represented by d-dimensional cycles. Choose a d-cycle Z on Y representing alpha. For a field extension M/k, let Y_M = X_M x_M X_M and let Z_M be the d-cycle on Y_M obtained from Z by flat base change, i.e. the sum of the integral components of dimension d of Z x_k M with scheme-theoretic multiplicities. The flat pullback of alpha to M is the class of Z_M in CH^d(Y_M).

Assume the flat pullback of alpha to L is zero. Then the class of Z_L in CH^d(Y_L) is zero. By the definition of rational equivalence, the subgroup R_d(Y_L) of Z_d(Y_L) is generated by cycles of the form i_* div(f), where i: W -> Y_L is a closed immersion of an integral closed subvariety W of Y_L of dimension d+1 and f is a nonzero rational function on W. Since [Z_L] = 0, there are finitely many such pairs (W_j, f_j), j=1,...,s, such that Z_L = sum_j i_{j,*} div(f_j) as d-cycles on Y_L. If d=0 there are no W_j and the sum is empty; the same argument below still works.

Each W_j is a closed subscheme of the finite type L-scheme Y_L, hence is cut out by finitely many equations on affine charts of Y_L. Each f_j is a quotient of regular functions on some affine open of W_j. Choose affine charts and equations, and let S be the finite set of elements of L occurring as coefficients in these equations and in the numerator and denominator of each f_j. Put L_0 = k(S). Then L_0 is a finitely generated field extension of k and L_0 is contained in L.

Because the data are defined over L_0, there exist integral closed subvarieties W_{j,0} of Y_{L_0} of dimension d+1 and nonzero rational functions f_{j,0} on W_{j,0} such that W_j = W_{j,0} x_{L_0} L and f_j is the base change of f_{j,0}. The subvariety W_{j,0} is integral because its base change to L is integral and L_0 -> L is a flat extension of fields; if two elements of its coordinate ring multiplied to zero, the same would be true after base change, forcing one to be zero. Its dimension is d+1 because dimension is preserved under flat base change. Let i_{j,0}: W_{j,0} -> Y_{L_0} be the closed immersion. The divisor of a rational function commutes with flat base change, and for a closed immersion pushforward is just taking the image with the same multiplicity, so the base change to L of i_{j,0,*} div(f_{j,0}) is i_{j,*} div(f_j). Therefore the base change to L of the d-cycle W := sum_j i_{j,0,*} div(f_{j,0}) on Y_{L_0} is sum_j i_{j,*} div(f_j) = Z_L.

Also the base change to L of Z_{L_0} is Z_L. Now apply the proved lemma eoinm/172653a31514f511/b03027 with E = L_0, L = L, Y = Y_{L_0}, and r = d. It asserts that the homomorphism Z_d(Y_{L_0}) -> Z_d(Y_L) sending an integral d-dimensional closed subscheme V to the associated d-cycle V_L is injective. Since W and Z_{L_0} have the same image Z_L, we obtain W = Z_{L_0} in Z_d(Y_{L_0}).

The cycle W is a finite sum of the standard generators of the rational equivalence subgroup R_d(Y_{L_0}); hence W = 0 in CH^d(Y_{L_0}). Since Z_{L_0} = W, the class of Z_{L_0} in CH^d(Y_{L_0}) is zero. This is exactly the statement that the flat pullback of alpha to CH^d(X_{L_0} x_{L_0} X_{L_0}) is zero.

Finally apply the proved lemma eoinm/172653a31514f511/b3e5b6 to the finitely generated field extension L_0/k. It gives an integer r >= 0 and elements t_1,...,t_r in L_0 that are algebraically independent over k such that L_0 is a finite extension of F = k(t_1,...,t_r). Since L_0 is contained in L, F is contained in L and L_0 is a finite extension of F contained in L. Let X/k be smooth projective of dimension d, let L/k be a field extension, and let alpha in CH^d(X x_k X) with integral coefficients, and suppose the flat pullback of alpha to CH^d(X_L x_L X_L) is zero. Step 2 (E/k is finitely generated). Because E/F is finite, let m = [E:F] >= 1 and choose an F-basis e_1,...,e_m of E. We claim E = k(t_1,...,t_r, e_1,...,e_m).

The field k(t_1,...,t_r, e_1,...,e_m) is the smallest subfield of L containing k together with t_1,...,t_r and e_1,...,e_m; since E is a field containing all of these elements, it contains that smallest field. Hence k(t_1,...,t_r, e_1,...,e_m) subseteq E.

Second inclusion, E subseteq k(t_1,...,t_r, e_1,...,e_m): take any x in E. Since e_1,...,e_m is an F-basis of E, x has a unique expression x = c_1 e_1 + ... + c_m e_m with c_i in F = k(t_1,...,t_r).
